title: Goldberg shows that floating-point addition need not be associative
summary: Goldberg shows that floating-point addition need not be associative.
body: David Goldberg's paper, in the text hosted by Oracle's Numerical Computation Guide, says that because of roundoff errors the associative laws of algebra do not necessarily hold for floating-point numbers. The expression (x+y)+z can have a different answer from x+(y+z). The source says: "Due to roundoff errors, the associative laws of algebra do not necessarily hold for floating-point numbers." A result that depends on the order of additions can change when the code is rearranged, even though real-number algebra would not notice. The paper is about IEEE-style floating-point arithmetic. It is not a claim that integer arithmetic fails in the same way.

sources.title: What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic
sources.author: David Goldberg
